cards.title: Ready on My Terms
cards.instruction: Agree to be honest, hopeful, or vulnerable only in forms that preserve your emotional safety.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll talk about the argument, but not the whole year tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole year matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It does. Tonight I can finish one sentence without leaving.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Where do we start?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With the argument, and permission to pause.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll talk about last night's rent argument, but not the whole year tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole year matters. You've been pulling away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It does. One question, and let me finish before you answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. Were you going to move out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I packed a bag. It's still upstairs. Please let that be the whole answer for a minute.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 agrees to discuss one argument under a scope limit; A3 and A5 explicitly preserve the ability to remain and pause.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 acknowledges B2's whole-year concern while limiting capacity; A5 answers B4's starting-point question with topic and safety condition.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the broader history recognized, then B4 cooperates in finding a manageable start.

heightening.evidence: A5 adds permission to pause but mostly consolidates A1's existing boundary.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes an argument discussion tonight, and A3's risk of leaving makes the immediate limit playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's single sentence and A5's permission to pause express the emotional condition without explanatory padding.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 limits the conversation's scope, A3 negotiates one uninterrupted question, and A5 discloses the packed bag while requiring a pause.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's year-long concern causes A3 to permit a question under safer conditions; B4's moving-out question elicits A5's concrete admission.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the sustained withdrawal addressed and B4 uses the negotiated opening to ask the consequential question.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves from procedural limits to admitting a bag remains packed upstairs, then preserves safety by limiting immediate follow-up.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes last night's rent argument; B2 supplies ongoing withdrawal and A5 locates the packed bag upstairs.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's short admission and request for a minute are economical and sincere, but the exchange offers little comic turn.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 insists the larger history matters; A3 acknowledges it and permits one question while controlling interruption.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 asks whether A intended to move out; A5 answers with the packed bag and negotiates time to tolerate that disclosure.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 each make openness conditional on a specific protection against emotional overload.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 increases the disclosure's stakes while retaining a narrower temporal boundary; the requested minute does not force the scene to end.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D119 makes A agree to emotional openness only within conditions that preserve A's sense of safety.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Avoidance refuses engagement; A offers a limited, feasible form of engagement and specifies the protection it requires.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A3 limits the exchange to one uninterrupted answer; after B4 accepts and asks about departure, A5 admits packing a bag while requesting time before further discussion.

records.recommendedEdit: Revised the rejected ending so protected openness occurs in speech. Added a rent argument and possible move to the existing year-long dispute. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A3 and A5 preserve safety while answering), logic 5 (B2's larger concern prompts one-question terms; B4's accepted terms and departure question cause A5's bag admission), relationship 4 (B2 seeks the broader truth and B4 accommodates limits), heightening 4 (A5 reveals an actual preparation to leave), specificity 5 (A1 rent and A5 upstairs bag), brevity/wit 3 (A5 is direct and playable but lightly comic); total 90. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words; hard gates pass. Downstream attribution remains separately unresolved.
records.remainingConcern: This is stronger as a vulnerable dramatic exchange than as comedy. Its exact behavioral progression is clear enough to pass without a rewrite.
records.writerReservation: The scene is primarily emotionally tense rather than comic. Its revised transcript cannot replace the supplied versioned seed snapshot without a separate provenance decision.
records.alternativeComparison: This alternative negotiates scope and conversational turns under direct questioning; the door-seat alternative uses an available exit and reassurance to enable a voluntary admission.

cards.title: Ready on My Terms
cards.instruction: Agree to be honest, hopeful, or vulnerable only in forms that preserve your emotional safety.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll sit by the door while we talk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you planning to run?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Knowing I can leave is helping me stay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can stop when you need to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Now I can risk a less careful answer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll sit by the door while we talk about trying again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you planning to run?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Knowing I can leave is helping me stay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can stop when you need to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want to come home. Please don't hand me a key yet; saying it is enough for tonight.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 explicitly makes the ability to leave the condition for staying, and A5 risks greater honesty after B4 supplies safety.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 corrects B2's interpretation of the door seat; A5 directly uses B4's permission to stop.

relationship.evidence: B2 fears departure and B4 responds with an accommodation that changes A's willingness to speak.

heightening.evidence: A5 advances from arranging a safe seat to risking a less guarded answer because of B4.

specificity.evidence: A1's door-side seat provides a concrete safety condition, though the conversation's topic remains open.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Knowing I can leave is helping me stay' expresses the character's paradox directly and economically.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 requires a door-side seat, A3 explains escape as the condition for staying, and A5 separates admitting a wish from accepting a key.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 directly answers B2's fear that A will run; B4's permission to stop enables A5's wish to come home with a new limit.

relationship.evidence: B2 reveals anxiety about A leaving, while B4 offers control over stopping so the reconciliation conversation can continue.

heightening.evidence: After B4 assures safety, A5 risks naming the desired reconciliation but protects against immediately making it concrete through a key.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a reconciliation conversation and chosen seat; A5's home and key make the stakes tangible, though their history remains broad.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Knowing I can leave is helping me stay' is economical; A5 earns its boundary but supplies limited comic surprise.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 interprets the seat as preparation to flee; A3 explains that the option to leave makes continued participation possible.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 grants permission to stop; A5 consequently volunteers a vulnerable wish while withholding permission for immediate practical commitment.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A's protective conditions shift from physical location in A1 to the pace of reconciliation in A5.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 reveals a larger hope and creates a correspondingly specific safeguard. 'Enough for tonight' expresses A's boundary rather than prescribing a fixed performance ending.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D119 makes A's willingness to be vulnerable depend on an emotionally safe form of participation.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Planning an escape aims at departure; A uses the available exit to make continued engagement possible.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A3 explicitly explains that exit access enables staying; B4's stopping permission then enables A5 to admit wanting to come home without committing to the key.

records.recommendedEdit: Preserved the door-seat causal exchange and specified reconciliation in A1. Replaced the rejected promise of a future answer with actual vulnerability and a further protective condition. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A3 exit access and A5 no immediate key), logic 5 (A3 corrects B2; B4's stopping permission enables A5's wish without commitment), relationship 4 (B2 fears departure and B4 accommodates A), heightening 4 (A5 admits wanting home while limiting the next step), specificity 4 (A1 reconciliation and A5 key establish the stakes without a separation history), brevity/wit 4 (A5 wanting home while postponing its key extends A3's paradox); total 90. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words; hard gates pass. Seed provenance is assessed separately.
records.remainingConcern: The key is introduced only in A5, although coming home makes it intelligible. The tone is primarily tender rather than witty. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A5's key condition assumes returning home would be a consequential next step, while leaving B free to respond. The revised transcript differs from the supplied versioned supporting seed.
records.alternativeComparison: Here B's reassurance opens voluntary vulnerability; the rent-argument alternative uses a negotiated question to elicit an admission about an existing plan to leave.
